target.title: docs(coding-agent): require fresh project worktrees
target.body:
## Summary

- require the bundled coding-agent launcher to prepare and verify an isolated worktree from freshly fetched canonical upstream state before a delegated worker edits a Git-backed project
- preserve the fetched contributor head and avoid automatic history rewrites for trusted existing PR/shared-branch work
- treat contributor-controlled refs as untrusted: never launch a permission-bypassed worker directly in those checkouts; use the repository-approved untrusted-PR sandbox/review workflow or stop
- keep read-only tasks and non-project scratch scaffolds exempt
- limit the final scope to `skills/coding-agent/SKILL.md`; there are no `AGENTS.md`, workspace-template, system-prompt, runtime/protocol, or skill-availability changes

## Verification

- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern -- skills/coding-agent/SKILL.md`
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- final `$autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main` with Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` at high reasoning: clean, no accepted/actionable findings
- pre-push canonical ancestry: `upstream/main` `125ad94d6d4be543a96a8d92b44bcf7869d37b7a` is an ancestor of pushed head `c23f427ef515e1205e26da45dca6d2fda30f4e40`; the fork head was also an ancestor and the update was pushed without force

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Delegated coding workers must start in launcher-prepared isolated worktrees based on freshly fetched canonical state when modifying a Git-backed project.

Real environment tested: OpenClaw source checkout with live canonical `openclaw/openclaw` and fork remotes, including a concurrently updated existing PR branch.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Fetched `upstream`, verified canonical ancestry and fork-head ancestry, integrated both without rewriting history, then pushed the existing PR branch without force.

Evidence after fix: The live PR diff contains only `skills/coding-agent/SKILL.md` and the pushed branch contains both the fetched canonical base and the concurrent fork head.

Observed result after fix: New project work requires a launcher-prepared fresh-canonical worktree; existing trusted branches preserve their fetched head; untrusted contributor refs are blocked from permission-bypassed launch; scratch/read-only work remains exempt.

What was not tested: A live model turn invoking the bundled coding-agent skill.
